items.description:
Let $X$ be a set and $h\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$ be any function. Then
\[
\mathcal{B}(\ell_2(X))^{\sigma_h}=\mathrm{C}^*_u(X,d_h).
\]
More generally, if $A\subseteq\mathcal{B}(\ell_2(X))$ is a $\sigma_h$-invariant
$\mathrm{C}^*$-subalgebra, then $A^{\sigma_h}$ is the closure of the operators
in $A$ with finite $d_h$-propagation.\label{thmA}
items.notes: Both the ambient Roe equality and the invariant closed complex star-subalgebra equality are proved for arbitrary X and h. The subalgebra need not be unital. Forward direction uses checked Fejer approximation; reverse direction uses checked de la Vallee Poussin reproduction and L1 continuity of its translations.

items.description:
\label{thmB}
Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space. Then
\[
\mathrm{C}^*_{ql}(X)=\mathrm{CP}(X)\quad\text{and}\quad \mathrm{C}^*_u(X)=\mathrm{AP}_{\exp}(X).\]
Moreover, if $X$ has at most exponential growth, then $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)=\mathrm{AP}(X)$.
items.notes: Full conjunction, with the manuscript metric and uniform-local-finiteness hypotheses: quasi-local=CP, Roe=AP_exp, and exponential growth implies Roe=AP. All supporting proof chains are checked; no external hypotheses are assumed.

items.description:
\label{thmC}
Let $X$ be a coarse disjoint union of expander graphs. Then
\[
\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)\subsetneq \mathrm{AP}_{\mathrm{strip}}(X)\subsetneq \mathrm{C}^*_{ql}(X).
\]
items.notes: Full unconditional source theorem for raw expander graph-union data, including empty initial components: Roe is strictly contained in AP_strip, which is strictly contained in quasi-local. Actual complex good subspaces, projections, bounded-product embedding and Ozawa nonembedding are all proved in the project. No cited or external mathematical assumption remains.

items.description:
\label{thmD}
Let $X$ be a coarse disjoint union of expander graphs. Then
\[
\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)\subsetneq \mathrm{QL}_{\exp}(X)\subsetneq \mathrm{QL}_\beta(X)\subsetneq \mathrm{QL}_\alpha(X)\subsetneq \mathrm{C}^*_{ql}(X)
\]
for all $0<\alpha<\beta$. Moreover, $\prod_n\mathrm{M}_n$ embeds into
$\mathrm{QL}_{\exp}(X)$.
items.notes: Full unconditional source theorem for every0<alpha<beta and raw expander graph-union data: Roe<QL_exp<QL_beta<QL_alpha<quasi-local, together with the injective isometric bounded complex matrix-product embedding into QL_exp. Empty initial components are removed by a checked relabeling on the same metric space.

items.description:
\label{thmE}
Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space. Then
$\mathrm{AP}_{\mathrm{strip}}(X)\subseteq \mathrm{QL}_{\exp}(X)$. If moreover
$X$ is a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs, then
$\mathrm{AP}_{\mathrm{strip}}(X)= \mathrm{QL}_{\exp}(X)$.
items.notes: Full forward inclusion for uniformly locally finite metric spaces and equality whenever a CoarseGraphUnion witness exists. The witness records a countable partition into finite connected graphs, exact shortest path metrics on each fiber, and separation as the sum of component indices tends to infinity. The reverse inclusion uses checked component moments, cut averaging for the off-block remainder, scalar normalization, and norm closure. No auxiliary analytic estimates, compactness facts, external results, or extra regularity hypotheses are assumed.

items.description: Let $(X,\cE)$ be a coarse space. The \emph{uniform Roe algebra of $X$}, denoted by $\cstu(X,\cE)$, is the norm closure of the set of all operators in $\cB(\ell_2(X))$ with controlled propagation. We simply write  $\cstu(X)$ if $\cE$ is clear from the context.
items.notes: Exact norm closure of controlled operators, bundled as a closed unital complex star-subalgebra for arbitrary coarse spaces.

items.description: Let $(X,\cE)$ be a coarse space. The set of all quasi-local operators in $\cB(\ell_2(X))$ forms a \cstar-algebra called the   \emph{quasi-local algebra of $X$}, denoted by $\cstql(X,\cE)$. If $\cE$ is clear from the context, we simply write $\cstql(X)$.
items.notes: Full complex unital star-subalgebra structure and norm closedness for arbitrary coarse spaces. Multiplication uses a projection splitting and relational composition of entourages; no metric or local finiteness is assumed.

items.description:
\label{Remark.C.d.u.}
    In view of the previous paragraph, we emphasize that, given a coarse disjoint  union $X=\bigsqcup_nX_n$ where each $X_n$ is a finite connected graph,  we can always change its metric in a way that the metric in each $X_n$ does not change and so that the rate of growth of $d(X_n,X_m)$ as $n+m\to \infty $ with $ n\neq m$ is as fast as we wish. Any such change does not impact the coarse type of the space. This is relevant for Subsection \ref{Subsection.exp.growth} since we would like to guarantee that u.l.f.\ coarse disjoint unions are bijectively coarsely equivalent to metric spaces with at most exponential growth (see Definition \ref{Defi.Exp.Growth}).
items.notes: For any prescribed real sequence rho, constructs a metric on the same set with unchanged internal component distances and cross distances at least rho(n+m), retaining coarse equivalence. Uses cumulative nonnegative weights added only between different components.

items.description:
\label{Lemma.support.ThetaKsa}
Let $X$ be a set, $h\colon X\to \R$ be a map, and $a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))$. Then, for each $s>0$, $\Theta_{h,K_s}(a)$ has $d_h$-propagation at most $s$.
items.notes: Every coefficient vanishes when |h(x)-h(y)|>s, giving the stated propagation bound at the same scale. Arbitrary X and h.

items.description:
\label{Lemma.ThetaKs(a).tends.to.a}
    Let $X$ be a set and $h\colon X\to \R$ be a map. If $a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))^{\sigma_h}$, then \[a=\lim_{s\to \infty}\Theta_{h,K_s}(a).\]
items.notes: Operator-norm convergence at positive infinity. Proved by changing variables to the fixed K_1 kernel and using dominated convergence; no explicit integrated-tail estimate is assumed.

items.description:
\label{PropLargestCoarseStrucWithhCoarse}
      Let $(X,\cE)$  be  a coarse space and $h\colon X\to\R$ be a function. Then $(X,\cE_h)$ is the largest  coarse substructure of $\cE$ such that $h\colon (X,\cE_h)\to \R$ is coarse. \qed

items.notes: Arbitrary coarse space and real h. Fejer averaging preserves support, imposes bounded h-variation, and is norm continuous. Closure and Theorem A give both inclusions.

Full equality for arbitrary coarse spaces and arbitrary real height maps. Fejer averages preserve each exact quasi-local tolerance/entourage. The finite-height-propagation step uses the checked three-band estimate and finite subcompression criterion; closure supplies the result. No local finiteness, metric, or continuity assumptions are added.

Full sharp estimate with constants 4 and 2. Finite orthogonal bands, floor rounding, and the perturbation estimate are proved in the project. Holds for arbitrary relations, without requiring controlledness, and nonnegative epsilon.

Full arbitrary coarse-space statement, with the actual bounded oscillation on an entourage, every s>2*pi*omega/delta, and exact error 16*delta*norm(a)+8*delta^(-1)*epsilon. A cosine square-partition and finite-sign orthogonality construct the bounded smoothing operator; no countability, Hilbert-valued measurability, or probabilistic assumption is needed.

items.description:
\label{Thm.Quasi-LocalContainedContinuityPoints}
    Let $(X,\cE)$ be a   coarse space. Then $\cstql(X,\cE)\subseteq \CP(X,\cE)$.
items.notes: Full inclusion for arbitrary coarse spaces. Uses the sharp commutator estimate on normalized real and imaginary parts of the diagonal phases and an explicit epsilon-delta argument. No smoothing lemma or external mathematical hypothesis is assumed.

items.description:
\label{RemarkContPointsCoarseSpaces}
    Notice that the inclusion in Theorem \ref{Thm.Quasi-LocalContainedContinuityPoints} is in general strict, even for u.l.f.\ coarse spaces.  Indeed, let $\cE_{\max}$ be the maximal u.l.f.\ coarse structure on $\N$, i.e., 
    \begin{align*}E&\in \cE_{\max}\ \Leftrightarrow\ \\
    &\sup_{n\in\N}\max\{|\{m\in \N\mid (n,m)\in E\}|,|\{m\in \N\mid (m,n)\in E\}|\}<\infty.\end{align*}Then $h\colon (\N,\cE_{\max})\to \R$ is coarse if and only if $h$ is bounded.  But then $\cB(\ell_2(\N))^{\sigma_h}=\cB(\ell_2(\N))$ for all coarse maps $h\colon \N\to \R$. On the other hand,  $\cstql(\N,\cE_{\max})$ is strictly smaller than $\cB(\ell_2(\N))$.
items.notes: Full source remark on literal naturals: constructs the maximal uniformly locally finite coarse structure and proves maximality. Coarse real functions are exactly bounded functions, so all operators are common continuity points. An explicit flat-row operator fails quasi-locality for every ULF coarse structure, proving the strict inclusion. No nonembedding theorem is used.

items.description:
Let $i,j\in\Z$ be such that $\chi_{A_i}a\chi_{B_j}\neq 0$. Then
    \[|i-j|\leq 1\ \text{ and }\ (A_i\times B_j)\cap F=\emptyset.\]
items.notes: Both source conclusions are proved: nonzero compression forces adjacent integer bands, and their rectangle misses the height-restricted entourage. Arbitrary sets and a positive height propagation bound are retained.

items.description:
\label{PropNotInQLThereisCoarseNotInCPFlow}
    Let $(X,d)$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space. If $a\not\in \cstql(X)$, then there is a coarse map $h\colon X\to \R$ such that $a\not\in \cB(\ell_2(X))^{ \sigma_h}$.
items.notes: Full non-quasi-local detection proposition. Finite compressions witness norm lower bounds; deleting finite rows/columns changes the operator by a Roe operator; recursion outside finite neighborhoods gives separated blocks. A checked Lipschitz extension and compression lower bound give the discontinuous coarse flow. Proved even for pseudometric spaces with the stated uniform finite-ball bounds.

items.description: For all $r>0$ and all finite $F\subseteq X$, there are finite $A,B\subseteq X\setminus F$ such that $d(A,B)>r$ and $\|\chi_Aa\chi_B\|\geq \eps/2$.
items.notes: Uniform positive compression lower bounds survive deletion of any finite buffer. The initial existential epsilon is rescaled by one half. The formulation allows all real radii and uses pointwise separation ≥R; taking R=r+1 supplies the source strict separation >r. All finite witnesses and error estimates are proved, without assuming compactness results.

items.description:
\label{Cor.cstql=CP.metric}
    Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space. Then, $\cstql(X)=\CP(X)$.
items.notes: Both inclusions checked. The forward inclusion holds for all coarse spaces; the reverse uses uniformly locally finite metric spaces, with a proof valid also for pseudometrics.

items.description:
\label{Def.BandAnalytic.functions}
Let $X$ be a set,    $a\in\cB(\ell_2(X))$,  $h\colon X\to \R$, and $\delta>0$. We say that $a$ is \emph{analytic on a strip of width $\delta$ for $\sigma_h$} if   there is a continuous map \[F\colon\{z\in\C\mid |\mathrm{Im}(z)|\leq\delta\}\to\cB(\ell_2(X))\] which is holomorphic on the interior of the strip  $\{z\in\C\mid |\mathrm{Im}(z)|\leq\delta\}$ and satisfies \[F(t)=\sigma_{h,t}(a)\ \text{ for all }\ t\in\R.\]
We say that  $a$ is \emph{analytic on a strip   for $\sigma_h$} if there is $\delta>0$ such that $a$ is analytic on a strip of width $\delta$ for $\sigma_h$. If the analytic extension  $F$ can be defined on the entire complex plane, we simply say that $a$ is \emph{analytic for $\sigma_h$}. In this case, we also say that $a$ is \emph{analytic on a strip of infinite width for $\sigma_h$}. Finally, if moreover there are $C,K>0$ such that the map $F$ above satisfies
\[\|F(z)\|\leq Ce^{K|\mathrm{Im}(z)|}\ \text{ for all }\ z\in \mathrm{dom}(F),\]
then the analyticity of $a$ for $\sigma_h$ is said to be of \emph{exponential type}.
items.notes: Positive-width strip, some-strip and strip exponential-type predicates now supplement the existing entire-extension and entire exponential-type predicates. Finite-strip norm boundedness proves strip analyticity equivalent to the finite-strip exponential-type condition; the entire exponential-type condition remains distinct.
Exact norm closure of the intersection of entire exponential-type points over all coarse real maps. The following closed unital complex star-subalgebra claim is separately verified.
Full closed-strip formula, including boundary, for arbitrary X and real h. Checked scalar identity theorem and continuity at the boundary.

Both directions for arbitrary X and real h, without local finiteness or boundedness of h. The reverse construction has the sharp norm bound ||a|| exp(M |Im z|). Finite forms are extended by density and Riesz representation; scalar Schwarz estimates and Cauchy integrals prove operator-valued holomorphy.

items.description:
It is worth pointing out that the implication \eqref{Item.Prop.analitic.iff.finite.dh.prop.3}$\Rightarrow$\eqref{Item.Prop.analitic.iff.finite.dh.prop.1}  of Proposition \ref{Prop.analitic.iff.finite.dh.prop} is much simpler if $a$ has finite $d$-propagation for a u.l.f.\ metric $d$ on $X$ and $h$ is coarse with respect to $d$. Indeed, in this scenario, if $a$ has finite $d$-propagation, then there are finitely many $E_1,\ldots, E_n\subseteq X\times X$ such that each $E_i$ is the graph of a partial translation\footnote{Given a metric space $(X,d)$, a partial translation $f$ of $X$ is a partial bijection of $X$, say $f\colon A\to B$ where $A,B\subseteq X$,  such that $\sup_{x\in A}d(x,f(x))<\infty$.} of $X$ and
\[\{(x,y)\in X\times X\mid d(x,y)\leq \mathrm{prop}(a)\}=E_1\sqcup\ldots\sqcup E_n.\]
Therefore, we can write $a=\sum_{i=1}^na_iv_{f_i}$ for  appropriate $a_i$'s in $\ell_\infty(X)$ and partial translations $f_i$'s.\footnote{If $f$ is a partial translation of $X$, $v_f$ is the partial isometry on $\ell_2(X)$ such that $v_f\delta_x=\delta_{f(x)}$ for all $x\in \dom(f)$ and $v_f\delta_x=0$ for all other $x$'s. Clearly, $v_f$ has finite propagation.} It is then easy to show that each $a_iv_{f_i}$ is analytic of exponential type for $\sigma_h$; this can be done by following the proof of    \cite[Proposition 1.4(2)]{BragaExel2023}.  Moreover, this weaker statement is in fact all we will use below. We chose to present the more elaborate statement of Proposition \ref{Prop.analitic.iff.finite.dh.prop}  since it seems to be the correct characterization.
items.notes: Full finite partial-translation decomposition for arbitrary uniformly locally finite coarse spaces. Controlled relations split into finitely many partial bijections; their operators have norm at most one and projection initial support. Bounded diagonal coefficients have norm at most norm(a). Each summand is entire of exponential type for every coarse real height, recovering the source metric claim. No sharp cardinal bound on the partition is asserted.

items.description: \label{lem:detect} Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space and let $(x_k)_k$ and $(y_k)_k$ be sequences in $X$ such that $\lim_kd(x_k,y_k)=\infty$.  Then there is an increasing sequence $(n_k)_k$ in $\N$ and a $1$-Lipschitz map $h\colon X\to\R$ such that \[|h(x_{n_{k}}) -h(y_{n_{k}})|\geq \frac{d(x_{n_k},y_{n_k})}{9}\ \text{ for all }\ k\in\N.\]
items.notes: Full 1/9 estimate and strictly increasing subsequence, proved for arbitrary pseudometric spaces. Uses individually oriented pairs and distance to their second endpoints, not Ramsey.

items.description: \label{cor:detect} Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space and suppose $a\in\B(\ell_2(X))$ has infinite propagation. Then there is a $1$-Lipschitz map $h\colon X\to\R$ such that $a$ has infinite $d_h$-propagation.
items.notes: Full detection of infinite propagation by a 1-Lipschitz real map, in arbitrary pseudometric spaces.
Full equivalence and consequent Roe=AP_exp equality are checked for arbitrary pseudometric spaces. The closure equality is separately registered.
Norm closure after intersecting all entire points over coarse real maps. Existence of an entire extension expresses the individual AP[X,h] membership.

items.description:
\label{Defi.Exp.Growth}
    Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space. For each $m\in\N\cup\{0\}$, let 
    \[N_X(m)=\sup_{x\in X}|B(x,m)|.\]
    We say that $X$ \emph{grows at most exponentially} if there is $\lambda>1$ such that \[N_X(m)\leq \lambda^m\ \text{ for all }\  m\in\N.\]
items.notes: The standalone volumeFunction is defined and the manuscript volume-function condition is proved equivalent to the existing uniform closed-ball predicate under uniform local finiteness. Positive natural radii preserve the manuscript convention.

items.description:
\label{Defi.21.sep.26.1.qqq}
Cayley graphs or, more generally, large scale geodesic spaces clearly grow at most exponentially. Also, while coarse disjoint unions of connected finite graphs with uniformly bounded degree may not, they are always bijectively  coarsely equivalent to spaces which are; see Remark \ref{Remark.C.d.u.}.
items.notes: Uniform local finiteness plus bounded-step chains whose lengths are bounded by an affine function of distance implies the exact exponential-volume condition. This standard large-scale-geodesic hypothesis allows multiplicative and additive constants. The connected shortest-path graph case and the bounded-degree coarse-union remetrization are separately checked, including the Cayley-graph special case under the paragraph’s uniform local finiteness convention.

Full source statement with N_X the supremum of closed-ball cardinalities and eta the supremum of coefficient norms at distance at least m. Includes the exact factor-two tail for every cutoff and Roe membership. Empty suprema use zero. The result allows pseudometrics and cutoff zero.

items.description:
\label{lem:allrates}
Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space and let $a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))$ be such that $a$ is analytic for $\sigma_h$ for all $1$-Lipschitz maps $h\colon X\to \R$.  Then \[\sup_{x,y\in X}e^{c\,d(x,y)}|\langle a\delta_y,\delta_x\rangle|<\infty\ \text{ for all }\ c>0.\]
items.notes: Every positive exponential rate has a uniform finite nonnegative coefficient bound. Entire extensions are assumed exactly for all 1-Lipschitz real maps, as in the source.

items.description:
\label{thm:roeentire.Exp.Growth}
Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space with at most exponential growth. Then
$
\cstu(X) =\mathrm{AP}(X)$.
items.notes: Full equality. Entire coefficient decay and uniform exponential closed-ball bounds give summable shell bounds; a checked Schur estimate proves operator-norm finite-propagation approximation. No cited partial-bijection decomposition is assumed.

items.description:
In the light of Theorem \ref{thm:roeentire}, it is natural to wonder if $\cstu(X)$ also equals $\mathrm{AP}_{\mathrm{strip}}(X)$,     the \cstar-subalgebra of $\cB(\ell_2(X))$ generated by the elements which are analytic on a strip for $\sigma_h$ for every coarse $h$.   Firstly, it is worth pointing out that the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:roeentire.Exp.Growth} fails to give that since, in order to use  Lemma \ref{lem:volume}, we need the
 imaginary parts of the elements in the domain of the extension $F$ to be arbitrarily large. Moreover, this is actually false in general and we show this in Theorems \ref{Thm.Exp.decay.Still.Contains} and \ref{Thm.Led.In.Band} below. Precisely, we show that, if $X$ is a coarse disjoint union of expander graphs, then $\mathrm{AP}_{\mathrm{strip}}(X)$ contains the product $\prod_n\mathrm M_n$.
items.notes: The literal bounded matrix-product embedding into AP_strip is proved for raw expander data by the constructed exponential embedding and the checked graph-union strip inclusion. No universal good-subspace premise remains.

items.description:
\label{Defi.QL.Decay.modulus}
    Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and $a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))$. The \emph{quasi-locality modulus of $a$} is the map $\eps_a\colon [0,\infty)\to [0,\infty)$ given by
    \[\eps_a(r)=\sup\left\{\|\chi_Aa\chi_B\|\mid A,B\subseteq X \text{ with } d(A,B)\geq r\right\}\]
    for all $r\geq 0$.

\label{Example.decay.uRa}
    Given a metric space $X$, an operator $a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))$ has finite propagation if and only if $\eps_a(r)=0$ for $r$ sufficiently large.

\label{Example.decay.ql}
    Given a metric space $X$, an operator $a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))$ is in the quasi-local algebra of $X$  if and only if $\lim_{r\to \infty}\eps_a(r)=0$.

\label{Defi.QLalpha}
    Let $(X,d)$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space and $\alpha\in (0,\infty)$.
    Given $a\in\cB(\ell_2(X))$, we say that $\eps_a$ has \emph{$\alpha$-polynomial decay} if $\eps_a(r)=O(r^{-\alpha})$, i.e., if there is $C>0$ such that \[\eps_a(r)\leq Cr^{-\alpha}\ \text{  for all }\ r>0.\] We define
    \[\mathrm{QL}_{\alpha}(X)=\overline{\left\{a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))\mid \eps_a(r)= O(r^{-\alpha})\right\}}^{\|\cdot\|}.\]
items.notes: Exact positive-radius bound by a positive constant times r^(-alpha), followed by norm closure. The closed star-subalgebra theorem assumes alpha>0 as in the manuscript.

items.description:
\label{Defi.QL.exp}
    Let $(X,d)$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space.
 Given $a\in\cB(\ell_2(X))$, we say that $\eps_a$ has \emph{exponential decay} if  there are $c,C>0$ such that
    \[\eps_a(r)\leq Ce^{-cr}\ \text{ for all }\ r\geq 0.\] We define
    \[\mathrm{QL}_{\exp}(X)=\overline{\left\{a\in \cB(\ell_2(X))\mid \eps_a\text{ decays exponentially}\right\}}^{\|\cdot\|}.\]
items.notes: Exact positive rate and positive constant bound for all nonnegative radii, followed by norm closure. Defined for arbitrary pseudometric spaces, including the manuscript metric case.

Unconditional full source statement for every finite complex coordinate set, including empty sets, with exact ceil(card^(1/4)) dimension and universal constant96. Uses the now-proved frame theorem with constant32 and exact appendix factor3.

items.description:
\label{Thm.Exp.decay.Still.Contains}
    Let $X$ be a coarse disjoint union of expander graphs. Then $\prod_n\mathrm M_n$ embeds into $\mathrm{QL}_{\exp}(X)$.
items.notes: Full unconditional bounded complex matrix-product embedding with exponentially decaying range, from literal raw expander data allowing empty initial components. Every quarter-power subspace is actually constructed. The homomorphism is injective and isometric.

Unconditional full strict decay chain for0<alpha<beta: QL_exp strictly inside QL_beta, strictly inside QL_alpha, strictly inside quasi-local. Actual Assumption.1 projections are constructed. The raw-expander adapter handles empty initial components on the same X.

Unconditional full source statement for every finite complex coordinate set and positive alpha satisfying the exact logarithmic size conditions. Closed subspace has exact floor(card/(log card)^alpha) dimension and universal constant32 in the compression estimate. No existence assumption remains.

items.description:
\label{Assumption.1}
    Let $X$ be a u.l.f.\ metric space which is the  coarse disjoint union of connected finite graphs, say $X=\bigsqcup_n X_n $. Assume that $\lim_n|X_n|=\infty$. Fix $\alpha>0$ and $n_0\in\N$ such that $n\geq n_0$ implies $1\leq(\log(|X_n|))^ {2\alpha}<|X_n|$. For each $n\geq n_0$, let $p_{n,\alpha}$ be a projection in $\cB(\ell_2(X_n))$ such that $\mathrm{rank}(p_{n,\alpha})$ is $\left\lfloor \tfrac{|X_n|}{(\log{(|X_n|)})^ {2\alpha}}\right\rfloor$ and
    \[
\|\chi_Ap_{n,\alpha}\|\leq C\sqrt{\frac{1}{(\log{(|X_n|)})^{2\alpha}}+\frac{|A|}{|X_n|}\log\left(\frac{e|X_n|}{|A|}\right)}
\]
for all nonempty $A\subseteq X_n$; the existence of such $p_{n,\alpha}$ and of such $C\geq 1$ is given by Lemma \ref{LemmaGoodSubspacesQuarterPower.LARGEDIM}. Define then
\[p_\alpha=\SOTh\sum_{n\geq n_0}p_{n,\alpha}.\]
So, $p_\alpha$ is a projection in $\prod_n\cB(\ell_2(X_n))$.
items.notes: Full unconditional construction of the source projections with universal constant32, exact logarithmic floor ranks for exponent2alpha, eventually admissible dimensions, zero initial components, block diagonal orthogonal projection and strong sum. Finite subspace existence is supplied by the checked good-subspace theorem, not assumed.

items.description:
\label{Prop.palpha.is.inQLalpha.exp}
   Assume the  setting of Assumption \ref{Assumption.1} and moreover that  $X=\bigsqcup_nX_n$ is a coarse disjoint union of expander graphs. Then,  $p_\alpha$ is in $\mathrm{QL}_\alpha(X)$.
items.notes: Full polynomial membership from the explicit projection data of Assumption.1, including arbitrary initial zero components and a single uniform modulus bound. Finite expander separation, the diameter/logarithm bound, entropy estimates and uniform component-to-ambient compression give HasPolynomialDecay. Actual existence of good finite subspaces is separate and is not asserted by this proposition.

items.description:
\label{lem:trace}
Let $H$ be a finite dimensional Hilbert space, $\delta\in (0,1)$, $p\in\B(H)$ be a projection, and $a\in\B(H)$ be self-adjoint with $\|a-p\|\leq \delta$. Then
\[
\mathrm{Tr}(a^{2m})\geq \rank(p)(1-\delta)^{2m}\ \text{for all}\  m\in\N.
\]
items.notes: Full finite-dimensional complex Hilbert-space result. The trace is exhibited as a real scalar with lower bound finrank(range p)*(1-delta)^(2m), for all natural m including zero. A checked finite spectral decomposition and finite Jensen inequality give the unit-vector estimate; Bessel bounds the sum over an orthonormal basis of the projection range. No spectral-measure axiom or external result is assumed.

items.description:
\label{lem:compression}
Let $X$ be a metric space,   $a\in\B(\ell_2(X))$, $x\in X$, $r>0$, $m\in\N$, and let $A=B(x,m r)$. Then
\[
\|a^m\delta_x\|\leq\|\chi_Aa\chi_A\|^m+m\|a\|^{m-1}\varepsilon_a(r).
\]
items.notes: Exact bound for all natural powers, including m=0. Localized vectors in expanding closed balls are controlled by the final ball compression; step errors accumulate with the exact factor m norm(a)^(m-1). Proved for arbitrary pseudometric spaces, hence covers the stated metric case.

items.description: \label{Thm.QLthetaDoesNotContainP} In the setting of Assumption \ref{Assumption.1}, $p_\alpha$ is not in $\mathrm{QL}_{\beta}(X)$ for any $\beta\in (\alpha,\infty)$.
items.notes: Full norm-closure nonmembership in the setting of Assumption.1. For a uniformly locally finite coarse graph union with diverging component sizes, any self-adjoint ambient operator whose eventual component restrictions are projections with the prescribed floor ranks and compression bounds lies outside polynomialQuasiLocal beta whenever 0<alpha<beta. These are the explicit projection data in Assumption.1; such projections are constructed unconditionally in ExpanderProjectionExistence. Uniform degree follows from uniform local finiteness. Self-adjoint approximants are obtained by realPart, component restriction preserves symmetry and contracts error/modulus, coordinate bases identify dimension with cardinality, and the assembled trace obstruction gives the contradiction. No decay, moment, radius or trace hypotheses beyond the manuscript setting remain.

items.description:
\label{Claim.ddd.q}
For  $n\geq n_0$ sufficiently large   and   $A\subseteq X_n$   nonempty with $|A|\leq k\sqrt{|X_n|}$, we have \[
\|\chi_Ap_{n,\alpha}\chi_A\|\leq C^2\left(\frac{1}{(\log(|X_n|))^ {2\alpha}}+\frac{k\log(e|X_n|)}{\sqrt{|X_n|}}\right).
\]
items.notes: Exact source operator bound from Assumption.1 at a nonempty finite subset with card A <= k sqrt(card X), for every card X > 1. Let $X$ be a set, $h\colon X\to\R$,    $a\in\cB(\ell_2(X))$ be analytic on a strip for $\sigma_h$, and let   $F$ witness this analyticity in the strip  $\{z\in \C\mid |\mathrm{Im}(z)|\leq \delta\}$, where   $\delta>0$.
 Then
 \[F(t+is)=\sigma_{h,t}(F(is))\] for all  $t\in\R$  and all  $\ |s|\leq\delta$. In particular,

items.description:
\label{Lemma.BandFromMoments}
Let $X$ be a set,  $h\colon X\to\R$ be a map, and  $a\in\cB(\ell_2(X))$ be such that $\ad_h^k(a)$ is bounded for all $k\in\N$. Assume      there are $A,B>0$ such that
\[\|\ad_h^k(a)\|\leq AB^kk!\ \text{ for all }\ k\geq0.\]
Then $a$ is analytic on  a strip for $\sigma_h$. Moreover,  this is the case for   any strip of width smaller than $ 1/B$.
items.notes: Full existence conclusion and every positive width δ<1/B, for arbitrary X and real h. A sequence of bounded operators realizes exactly the entrywise powers defining all iterated commutators, including order zero; factorial growth is the source assumption. Real-centered operator Taylor disks have radius at least 1/B and identical prescribed matrix coefficients, so they agree locally. This gives holomorphy throughout the open strip of width 1/B and continuity on every smaller closed strip. No higher-moment estimates or unproved analytic criteria are assumed. The proof does not need the separate A>0 assumption and therefore implies the stated positive-A case.

items.description: Lipschitz and differentiable orbit regularities define intermediate dynamical C*-algebras.
items.notes: Named examples are formalized precisely by norm-closing common Lipschitz, differentiable and real C^k orbit elements, k in Nat-infinity including smooth orbits. They form closed unital complex star-algebras between Roe and quasi-local for ULF metric spaces, and are bijective coarse invariants. No theorem for unspecified arbitrary regularity conditions is asserted. Closure is the convention used throughout the source analytic examples.

items.description: Polynomial and exponential decay algebras are not bijective coarse invariants in general.
items.notes: Actual counterexamples are constructed on a concrete metric expander family obtained from32 finite permutations with degree64 and expansion1/2. For everyalpha>0, square-root remetrization changes QL_alpha to the strictly larger oldQL_(alpha/2). Logarithmic remetrization strictly enlarges QL_exp. Both metrics are ULF and have exactly equal coarse structures. No expander-existence assumption is left open.

items.description: Entire analytic elements form a dense subalgebra for every C*-flow.
items.notes: General-flow density of the entire analytic complex star-subalgebra is proved for arbitrary possibly nonunital C*-algebras, by actual Gaussian convolution, differentiation under the integral, covariance and dominated-convergence approximation. The references to KMS theory describe historical use, without assuming an additional KMS theorem.

items.description: Parenthetical growth assertion for bounded-degree coarse graph unions.
items.notes: Author explicitly authorized adding the change-of-metric qualification on 2026-09-28. The remetrization theorem preserves the coarse structure and gives exponential growth. items.description: Property A implies uniform Roe equals quasi-local, so intermediate regularity algebras coincide.
items.notes: The complex Hilbert-space Property A application is proved directly: standard probability/l1 rows agree with the finite-kernel definition on ULF spaces, clipped finite-sign averages produce finite-propagation contractions at error18t, and norm closure gives Roe=quasi-local. Every intermediate algebra therefore equals Roe. No external theorem is assumed, and no claim is made to formalize broader Banach-space statements of the cited articles.
